args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money, per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`, but FIN-212 requires banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`). This caused the nightly build to fail on `tests/test_money.py`.

## Changes
- Replaced `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `src/money.py`.
- No test changes needed; existing tests now pass.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed (tests/test_money.py::test_half_even green).

Reviewer: @alex
args.head: fix/bankers-rounding-fin-212
args.title: Fix money rounding to use banker's rounding (FIN-212)

transcript.reasoning_content: Let me look at the repo files first.

transcript.content: The test confirms the expected behavior: `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (2.675 → 2.68, 2.665 → 2.66). The implementation currently uses `ROUND_HALF_UP`. I'll create a branch and fix it.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Wait — banker's rounding of 2.675 to cents: 2.675 → half-even → 2.68 (7 is odd, round up to 8). And 2.665 → 6 is even → stays 2.66. Correct.

Fix: import ROUND_HALF_EVEN and use it.
